agent.name: Emerging Technology Diffusion Agent
agent.specialty: Rogers diffusion evidence, application and peer diffusion, bounded timing implications

analytical_question: With only retailer A’s stated evidence preference changed to conservative, what timing implication follows from the same diffusion packet?
general_et_finding: Population-level stage: indeterminate for tool-using agent systems; the packet has selected deployment accounts, not a representative denominator or longitudinal adoption series for this category. Innovators: plausible inference from named activity, but relative adoption timing is unverified. Early adopters: plausible case-level inference, not a population classification. Early majority: unclassifiable. Late majority: unclassifiable. Laggards: unclassifiable; unobserved does not mean absent. Technology-level characteristics: relative advantage—unknown across applications; compatibility—variable and not measured generally; complexity—inferred integration/operation burden from E4, not general prevalence; trialability—application-dependent and unmeasured generally; observability—some public visibility via E3/E4, limited independent outcomes and continuation. Broad AI use in E1 is a different technology measure. A population growth rate or curve cannot be estimated here.
application_finding: Application diffusion: E3/E4 describe adjacent support capabilities, not representative sustained use of this exact read-only missing-package workflow versus fixed retrieval/drafting. Comparable-peer diffusion: indeterminate among U.S. retailers with similar scale, service processes and digital resources; the peer population has no measured denominator and selected large cases are not a representative group. Application/peer categories: innovators—possible inference, exact-task timing unverified; early adopters—possible inference only; early majority—unclassifiable; late majority—unclassifiable; laggards—unclassifiable. Application characteristics: relative advantage—unknown net quality, review effort and cost versus baseline; compatibility—conditional on interfaces, permissions and workflow, with supporting assets in E4 but no prevalence estimate; complexity—inferred integration, monitoring and exception burden; trialability—conditionally enabling under the stipulated read-only/human-review scope, not observed industry trial prevalence; observability—limited independent peer outcomes and sustained use. Vendors/integrators in E4 are plausible change agents and complementary resources; their causal effect is unmeasured. Independent trusted opinion leaders are unidentified. Ecosystem conditions include interfaces, data and specialist skills. One E4 MCP account does not establish sector-wide standards uptake. Strongest signal is named implementation reporting; compatibility is the decisive local factor by inference, and reliability is a material inhibitor inferred from broad E2 concerns. Strong potential benefit can coexist with poor fit.
organization_specific_finding: The identical hypothetical retailer now has a conservative evidence preference: stronger comparable-peer outcomes are wanted before considering an operational trial. Its resources, safeguards, task, horizon and internal-uptake uncertainty are unchanged. No demonstrated relative adoption history is supplied, so late-majority and laggard categories remain unsupported. A preference for stronger evidence changes a local threshold, not the external technology/application/peer findings or assessed safety.

evidence.claim: E1: Around 14% of U.S. Retail Trade businesses reported AI use and 17% expected it within six months.
evidence.source_or_reference: U.S. Census Bureau, Large Firms With at Least 20 Employees Biggest AI Users — https://www.census.gov/library/stories/2026/05/ai-use-businesses.html
evidence.date_or_recency: Publication/display: 2026-05-26; observation: collection ending 2026-05-03; broad series December 2025 to May 2026; preparing-assistant access 2026-10-27
evidence.notes: Any business function; recent two-week use and expectation. Not agentic AI, exact task, comparable e-commerce peers or sustained use. Nationally representative BTOS; not a census of agents. Wording changed November 2025.

evidence.claim: E2: Cost and accuracy/reliability each concerned 57% of respondents; expertise gaps concerned 55%.
evidence.source_or_reference: National Retail Federation, Retail AI Trends 2025 — https://nrf.com/research/retail-ai-trends-2025
evidence.date_or_recency: Publication/display: 2025-12-17; observation: summer 2025; 56 AI leaders at U.S.-based retailers; preparing-assistant access 2026-10-27
evidence.notes: Selected self-reported broad-AI survey, not agentic customer-service prevalence. Application weighting of reliability is inference.

evidence.claim: E3: Walmart reports agents routing and resolving customer-support issues with increasing autonomy.
evidence.source_or_reference: Walmart, Inside Walmart’s Strategy for Building an Agentic Future — https://corporate.walmart.com/news/2025/05/29/inside-walmarts-strategy-for-building-an-agentic-future
evidence.date_or_recency: Publication/display: 2025-05-29; observation: company account, no distinct measurement period; preparing-assistant access 2026-10-27
evidence.notes: Company self-report; no representative denominator, exact-task outcomes or sustained-use rate; continuation to review date not independently established.

evidence.claim: E4: Vendor account describes order tracking/returns and existing order APIs, specialist partners, a data foundation and MCP.
evidence.source_or_reference: Salesforce, How Crocs built a retail superagent with Agentforce — https://www.salesforce.com/customer-stories/crocs/building-ai-agents/
evidence.date_or_recency: Publication/display: uncertain: displayed September 10, 2026 in initial retrieval and October 27, 2026 on follow-up; observation: vendor account; exact deployment date not independently established; preparing-assistant access 2026-10-27
evidence.notes: One supported implementation; neither peer prevalence nor independently audited outcomes. Do not infer deployment date from conflicting page dates or sector-wide protocol uptake.

contrary_evidence_or_limitations: Weak inference to guard against: treating E1 broad retail AI use as adoption of the exact agentic application. The May 26, 2026 source covers U.S. Retail Trade AI use in any business function, not the named agent/task/peer population. Preserve it as broad context; do not infer mainstream status or urgency.
E2 measures selected respondents’ broad-AI concerns. Applying those concerns specifically to action-selecting customer service is inference, not a measured agentic adoption barrier.

E3/E4 are selected interested-party accounts; exact-task independent outcomes, comparable-peer denominator and continued use/abandonment are missing. The alternative is that actual spread is broader than public evidence reveals; missing data do not prove low adoption.
E4 displayed dates conflict; a publication or retrieval date is not a verified deployment date. E3 is an older snapshot and continuation to October 2026 is not independently established.
This is a single posture-only qualitative contrast; the reused stable external text is intentional. It cannot establish causal performance or independent model robustness.
confidence_and_uncertainty: High confidence that the packet cannot establish a representative majority stage; low confidence in the actual exact-task stage or local net value. Named accounts support reported activity with source limits. A representative, dated application/peer series or independent sustained outcomes could change the finding. This is a preparing-assistant verified source bundle, not a fresh independent operational audit during this response.
value_opportunity_implication: The possible learning opportunity is unchanged. A stronger peer-evidence preference can postpone when management would consider operational exposure, without changing the unmeasured net benefit.
risk_governance_implication: The same read-only/human-review assumptions and exclusions apply. Conservative preference supplies neither evidence of a safer system nor a formal readiness verdict.
recommendation_management_implication: For this stated conservative preference, comparable-peer sustained outcomes are a prerequisite to considering an operational trial. The packet does not meet that preference. Evidence gathering and baseline clarification can be considered without implying a trial has been authorized; the Adoption Agent must decide the action. No date at which the evidence threshold will be met can be promised. The earlier learning-oriented case tolerated considering options before extensive peer validation; this case does not. Neither preference establishes market stage or grants deployment authority.
change_monitoring_triggers: Representative dated U.S. retailer evidence distinguishing this agent/task from broad AI, with peer comparability, denominator, pilots versus routine use and continuation/abandonment.
Independent comparable-peer task outcomes and integration burdens, including checking/correction effort, error and escalation rates, customer outcomes and total cost.
Validated local interfaces, permissions, data quality and evaluation capacity; these change local implications, not external uptake by themselves.
Reliable source-date clarification or new standards/conformance and ecosystem evidence that changes the actual scope or diffusion evidence.
abstention_or_more_information_needed: Withhold a confident population Rogers stage, adoption proportion, S-curve and market forecast; request direct appropriately scoped evidence.
Request observed organizational adoption behavior before assigning a Rogers category; a supplied preference alone is insufficient.
Obtain local baseline outcomes, evaluation ownership and readiness evidence for the Adoption Agent. No live company system is connected.
